metadata.author: Jonathan Michael Retting
metadata.study: Identification of a Novel Druggable Pocket in the HIV-1 gp120 C5 Domain at the Conformational Relay Junction

method: Fragment merging + scaffold hopping + bioisosteric replacement, scored by pharmacophore complementarity and novelty

designs.name: RelayLead-02
designs.rationale: Benzoxazole-biphenyl linked to hydroxybenzyl piperazine. Benzoxazole provides H-bond accepting nitrogen for pocket donors. The phenol group addresses pocket acceptor features. Piperazine linker spans the pocket cleft.
designs.design_strategy: Fragment merging: benzoxazole H-bond + piperazine flexibility + phenol donor

designs.name: RelayLead-07
designs.rationale: Diaminopyrimidine-tetrahydrofuran: diamino pyrimidine provides 4 potential H-bond sites matching the pocket's high donor/acceptor density. THF ether provides a metabolically stable H-bond acceptor. Amide linker addresses central pocket HBA.
designs.design_strategy: Maximal H-bond density design to match the pocket's unusually high polar feature count

designs.name: RelayLead-08
designs.rationale: 4-Hydroxyquinolinone with fluorophenol piperidine. The quinolinone provides a rigid planar H-bond donor/acceptor surface for pocket engagement. The piperidine spacer provides optimal distance to the fluorophenol pharmacophore.
designs.design_strategy: Rigid core + flexible linker strategy for optimal pocket shape filling

designs.name: RelayLead-01
designs.rationale: Piperazine-indazole core (from BMS scaffold) with difluorophenol for enhanced H-bonding. The piperazine provides conformational flexibility to reach multiple pocket HBD/HBA features. Difluoro substitution improves metabolic stability.
designs.design_strategy: Scaffold hop from BMS-626529 benzimidazole to indazole + fluorinated phenol

designs.name: RelayLead-04
designs.rationale: Purine-piperazine core mimicking adenine recognition. The 7-deazapurine moiety provides dual H-bond donor/acceptor capability for simultaneous engagement with pocket donors and acceptors. Cyclopropyl amide provides metabolic resistance.
designs.design_strategy: Bioisosteric replacement: pyrimidine to 7-deazapurine for enhanced H-bond network

designs.name: RelayLead-05
designs.rationale: Quinolinol-sulfonylpiperazine: quinoline-2-ol provides strong H-bond donor and acceptor for pocket engagement. Sulfonamide linker adds two H-bond acceptors. Fluorophenyl provides hydrophobic anchoring. Novel topology not present in known entry inhibitors.
designs.design_strategy: New scaffold class: quinolinol + sulfonamide — unprecedented in HIV entry inhibitor space

designs.name: RelayLead-03
designs.rationale: Spirocyclic piperidine core provides 3D shape complementarity to the curved pocket surface. Nicotinamide arm addresses pocket donor features. Fluorophenyl provides hydrophobic contact and metabolic stability. Acetyl cap prevents excessive basicity.
designs.design_strategy: 3D-focused design with sp3-rich scaffold for pocket shape matching

designs.name: RelayLead-06
designs.rationale: Pyrimidinone-piperidine scaffold with methoxyphenyl. The pyrimidinone provides both H-bond donor (NH) and acceptor (C=O) capacity. Cyclopentyl improves metabolic stability and adds hydrophobic contact. Methoxyphenyl extends into the aromatic subpocket.
designs.design_strategy: Fragment growing from pyrimidinone core toward aromatic and hydrophobic pocket features
